title: Hierarchically Porous Unsubstituted Olefin‐Linked COF With Synergistically Enhanced Electronic and Ionic Conductivities for High‐Performance Lithium‐Ion Battery Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with synergistically enhanced ionic/electronic conductivities, improved active site utilization, and increased chemical stability for achieving high‐performance lithium–ion battery (LIB) cathodes remain a significant challenge. Here, we report the rational design of a novel unsubstituted olefin–linked, highly crystalline COF (namely HATN–ICTO COF) as a cathode for LIBs. The HATN–ICTO COF integrates extended fully conjugated π–networks, hierarchical porosity, and dual redox–active centers, enabling a synergistic improvement in ionic and electronic conductivity as well as a high theoretical capacity. This unique unsubstituted olefin linkage also endows the COF with excellent chemical stability, thereby ensuring long‐term cycling performance. Meanwhile, the hierarchical porous architecture of the COF can effectively buffer the volume expansion during repeated charge–discharge processes, mitigating electrode damage. The COF delivers a high specific capacity of 293 mAh g − 1 at 0.1 A g − 1 and maintains 206 mAh g − 1 at 10.0 A g − 1 , with outstanding cycling performance of 155 mAh g − 1 at 5.0 A g − 1 after 18,000 cycles. Additionally, a pouch cell based on the HATN–ICTO COF//Li configuration was also demonstrated. This work provides fundamental insights into structure–property relationships governing charge delocalization and redox activity in COFs.

title: Gradient‐Engineered Hole‐Selective Contact Layers via Spatially Confined Annealing for Efficient Tin–Lead and All‐Perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Hole‐selective contact layers (HSLs) govern charge extraction and interfacial energetics in perovskite solar cells, yet conventional designs are largely limited to planar architectures with homogeneous electronic properties. Such planar HSLs are insufficient for mixed tin–lead (Sn–Pb) perovskites, where short carrier diffusion lengths require efficient three‐dimensional charge‐collection pathways. Here, a spatially confined molecular‐gradient engineering strategy is introduced to construct energetic‐cascade HSLs within mesoporous frameworks. A screened and optimized phosphonic‐acid self‐assembled monolayer, [2‐(7H‐dibenzo[c,e]carbazol‐7‐yl)ethyl] phosphate, is incorporated into a mesoporous indium tin oxide nanocrystal matrix. Spatially confined annealing drives directional molecular redistribution, generating a controllable bottom‐to‐surface concentration gradient. This gradient establishes continuous energy cascades and graded hole‐transport channels, while simultaneously modulating the crystallization of the overlying Sn–Pb perovskite to suppress nonradiative recombination. Single‐junction Sn–Pb perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 24.14%, and monolithic two‐terminal all‐perovskite tandem solar cells reach 29.56% efficiency with substantially improved operational stability. More broadly, this work establishes molecular‐gradient engineering in porous matrices as a versatile strategy for programming charge transport and interfacial chemistry in solution‐processed optoelectronic devices.

title: Electronic Structure of Co-Phthalocyanine Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) composed of metal phthalocyanines (MPc; MPc-MOF) are predicted to possess electronic structures similar to those of Dirac materials, such as the Lieb lattice and the fes lattice. Therefore, in this study, we first investigated the energy band structure of CoPc-MOF using density functional theory (DFT). According to previous theoretical studies, if the lattice structure of CoPc-MOF is regarded as a Lieb lattice, its π-band is predicted to exhibit stronger Dirac-band-like characteristics compared to other MPc-MOFs containing metals. The electron density obtained from the energy band calculations indicated that the contribution of the central metal to the π-band of CoPc-MOF is small; therefore, the lattice structure can be assumed to be more similar to the fes lattice than to the Lieb lattice. Next, we evaluated the crystal structure of the synthesized CoPc-MOF using X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The TEM images revealed that the synthesized CoPc-MOF powder consists of flake-like microcrystals, in which crystal growth along the molecular layer stacking direction is minimal. Furthermore, the absorption spectra in the visible and near-infrared (Vis–NIR) regions indicate that CoPc-MOF is a narrow-gap semiconductor with an optical gap of approximately 0.36 eV. On the other hand, DFT calculations indicate that the CoPc-MOF crystal is metallic due to the formation of a π-band in the interlayer direction (along the c-axis), which is inconsistent with the experimental results. This suggests that the synthesized CoPc-MOF may not be sufficiently stacked in the interlayer direction. This finding is consistent with the TEM images, which show that CoPc-MOF consists of flake-like microcrystalline structures. Energy band calculations were performed on a single monolayer of CoPc-MOF; however, even a single monolayer of CoPc-MOF behaves as a metal when electronic correlations are not explicitly considered, which contradicts the Vis–NIR and UPS experimental results. The single molecular layer of CoPc-MOF exhibited a metallic ground state because the π-d bands near the Fermi level formed the Fermi surface. In conclusion, the DFT+U energy-band calculations for the CoPc-MOF monolayer reproduced a semiconducting ground state and best explained the UPS spectra. These results indicate that the electronic correlation effects are significant in the 2D π-d bands near the Fermi level of a single molecular layer of CoPc-MOF.

title: Multiscale Engineering of Three‐Phase Interfaces for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) offer high efficiency and zero‐emission operation, yet membrane electrode assembly performance is constrained by coupled oxygen, proton, electron, and water transport. This review summarizes advances in multiscale three‐phase interface engineering. At the nanoscale, catalyst protection, catalyst–ionomer interactions, molecular modifiers, and ionomer design improve active site accessibility and oxygen transport. At the electrode scale, support microenvironments and catalyst layer architectures regulate pore connectivity, wettability, ionomer distribution, electronic conduction, and water removal. At the device scale, structured assemblies, membranes, gas diffusion layers, microporous layers, and flow fields coordinate mass and charge transport under practical conditions. Future priorities include scalable fabrication, operando diagnostics, multiscale modeling, and AI‐assisted optimization. By integrating interfacial, electrode, and device engineering, this review provides a framework for developing durable, high‐power, low‐platinum PEMFCs and advancing automotive fuel cell stacks with improved performance, lifetime, and economic feasibility.

title: Atomic‐Scale Origin of Charge Density Wave–Driven Metal–Semiconductor Transition in an Incommensurately Modulated Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Although metal–organic frameworks are widely recognized for their long‐range crystalline periodicity, they can also exhibit intrinsic aperiodic structures associated with incommensurate modulation, whose observation has been exceptionally rare. In low‐dimensional condensed matter physics, these unique structures often give rise to novel physical phenomena such as charge density wave. However, owing to limited direct experimental evidence, the relationship between incommensurate structural modulation and temperature‐dependent electronic transport in conductive metal–organic frameworks remains incompletely understood. Here, using high‐quality Pr 3 HHTP 2 (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) single crystals as a model system, we resolve the incommensurately modulated structure at 100 K (modulation vector q = 0.39143(12) c * ) via temperature‐dependent single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction. The observed reversible metal–semiconductor transition near 350 K occurs in a similar temperature range to the disappearance of the structural modulation, supporting a connection between lattice distortion and electronic behavior. The modulation reappears upon cooling, with guest water molecules influencing both the extent of its recovery and the electrical conductivity of the material. This work establishes a concrete experimental criterion for one‐dimensional charge density wave in metal‐organic frameworks and provides an ideal platform for probing coupled electronic–lattice modulations.

title: Urchin-Like Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Lower Intraocular Pressure through PARP1 Inhibition
abstract: Abstract Elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) drives glaucoma progression, yet durable control is limited by incomplete mechanistic targeting and inefficient anterior-segment drug delivery. Here, we identify poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) hyperactivation as a redox-sensitive control node governing conventional outflow failure. In human trabecular meshwork and Schlemm’s canal tissues, upregulated PARP1, following oxidative stress, enforces nuclear retention of the ataxia telangiectasia mutated–NF-κB essential modulator (ATM–NEMO) complex. This suppresses cytoplasmic protein kinase B–endothelial nitric oxide synthase (AKT–eNOS) signaling and depletes intracellular nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), effectively coupling DNA damage responses to nitric oxide deficiency and metabolic collapse. To reprogram this dual enzymatic–metabolic disturbance, we engineer a geometry-enhanced, pH-gated urchin-like mesoporous nanoplatform (hereafter denoted PUON@NMOF) that enables spatially segregated codelivery of the PARP1 inhibitor niraparib and the NAD+ precursor nicotinamide mononucleotide. The spiny nanoarchitecture enhances corneal adhesion and trans-epithelial transport, while the metal–organic framework (MOF) shell provides switchable release under mildly acidic microenvironments. Topical administration achieves preferential accumulation in outflow tissues, restores NAD+ pools, reactivates AKT–eNOS signaling and produces synergistic IOP reduction across distinct glaucoma models. These findings define the redox–PARP1 axis as a druggable vulnerability and establish materials-enabled dual-pathway correction as a strategy for precision modulation of outflow biomechanics.

title: Is Adsorbed CO a Favorable Intermediate in Urea Electrochemical Synthesis on Copper Surfaces?
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical synthesis of urea from the co-reduction of CO2 and nitrate is limited by the sluggish C–N coupling process. On Cu surfaces, adsorbed CO (*CO), a species produced from CO2 reduction, is widely accepted as the key carbonaceous intermediate for C–N bond formation. However, a molecular-level understanding of how *CO participates in this process has not been fully obtained. Herein, we combine surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to study the C–N coupling process on polycrystalline Cu surfaces. The *CO coverage is systematically modulated by varying the nitrate concentration and CO2/CO atmosphere and correlated with the urea synthesis performance. In contrast to the previously proposed mechanism, we reveal that (1) *CO is neither the only nor the most favorable carbonaceous intermediate for urea generation. Depending on the exposed facet of Cu, C–N coupling involving the adsorbed COOH (*COOH) or CO2 (*CO2) with NO2 (*NO2) exhibits a lower kinetic barrier; (2) excessive surface coverage of *CO is detrimental to nitrate reduction and C–N coupling by blocking the active site. This work supplements a more comprehensive picture of the C–N coupling process in the electrochemical synthesis of urea and provides guidelines for the design of Cu-based electrocatalysts.

title: Supramolecular Hexaphyrin Cage: Cooperative Guest Binding and Reversible Aromaticity Switching by Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer
abstract: Abstract Coordination-driven self-assembly of a rigidified, antiaromatic β,β’-linked hexaphyrin ligand (1) bearing three meso-pyridyl donors with a trans-platinum(II) diacceptor corner (2) affords a discrete trigonal-prismatic metal–organic cage, CHP, in which two cofacial hexaphyrin decks are held rigidly apart by three Pt(II)-based coordination bridges. Multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, high-resolution ESI-MS, and DOSY establish the assembly as a single, highly symmetric [2 + 3] species, with a solution-state hydrodynamic radius consistent with the DFT-optimized geometry. Electrochemical and spectroelectrochemical studies reveal that CHP undergoes a reversible proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process, interconverting between a 24π-antiaromatic and a 26π-aromatic Hückel state upon combined treatment with a proton source and a mild chemical or electrochemical reductant, demonstrating that the switching behavior of the parent hexaphyrin is preserved within the confined 3D architecture. Furthermore, the electron-poor internal cavity of CHP encapsulates two planar zinc(II) porphyrazine guests in a discrete 1:2 host–guest complex with positive cooperativity, as quantified by UV–vis titration. This work establishes a strategy for embedding the electronic responsiveness of expanded porphyrinoids within discrete, functional supramolecular hosts.

title: Aqueous π‐Hole Interactions Enabled by Chiral Perfluoroarene Amphiphiles
abstract: ABSTRACT Arene‐perfluoroarene (AP) interactions, as a representative class of π‐hole‐driven noncovalent interactions, have demonstrated unique advantages in molecular recognition and supramolecular assembly. However, the precise regulation of hydrophobic aromatic molecules in aqueous environments through AP interactions remains challenging. Herein, we designed and constructed a series of chiral perfluoroarene amphiphiles based on an octafluoronaphthalene scaffold, in which the amphiphilicity, self‐assembly behavior, and confined microenvironment were regulated through end‐group engineering, enabling selective recognition and photophysical modulation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). These perfluoroarene amphiphiles readily formed stable lamellar vesicular assemblies in aqueous solution. The π‐hole region of the perfluoroarene moiety interacted with PAHs through AP interactions, facilitating the incorporation of guest molecules into the confined lamellar domains. Consequently, a variety of hydrophobic PAHs were successfully encapsulated in aqueous media, accompanied by effective modulation of their excited‐state behaviors. Moreover, the chiral confined microenvironment induced chiroptical responses from achiral PAHs, enabling efficient chirality transfer. This work provides a new design strategy for aqueous supramolecular recognition, aromatic guest aggregation regulation, and the construction of chiral photofunctional materials based on AP interactions.

title: Cryptochiral Circularly Polarized Luminescence Emerges From Cosolvent‐Regulated Pathway Complexity in Amyloidogenic Peptide Self‐Assembly
abstract: Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) is important for chiral photonics, optical encryption, bioimaging, and information processing. It is usually associated with an identifiable chiral ground‐state organization, and CPL without detectable ground‐state chirality remains comparatively unexplored. Herein, we report a rare “ cryptochiral CPL ” phenomenon arising from cosolvent‐regulated pathway complexity in the self‐assembly of a naphthalimide (NMI)‐amyloidogenic peptide conjugate (PEP‐L). In water, PEP‐L spontaneously forms thermodynamically stable, emissive nanofibers with pronounced supramolecular chirality and strong CPL. Adding a small amount of cosolvent redirects assembly toward kinetically trapped spherical nanoassemblies and shows no detectable Circular Dichroism (CD) response in the naphthalimide chromophore region, but retains pronounced CPL, which decouples ground‐state and excited‐state chiroptical responses. We term this behavior cryptochiral CPL . Thermal annealing or aging converts the spheres into thermodynamically favored nanofibers with distinct CD and CPL characteristics. The enantiomer PEP‐D shows mirror‐image chiroptical responses, which validates the phenomenon. Density functional theory (DFT) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations under different conditions give molecular‐level insight into the conformation, noncovalent interactions, and supramolecular organization of the different assembly states. These findings establish a new conceptual framework for adaptive chiral photonic materials and open opportunities for hidden optical encoding and biomolecular photonic systems.

title: Water-Soluble Pd12 Multicomponent Cage Enables Selective Separation of 1,4-Dibromonaphthalene from 1,5-Dibromonaphthalene and Regioselective Bromination of Naphthalene
abstract: Abstract The synthesis of intricate supramolecular architectures is driven by the desire to translate structural complexity into functional specificity. Herein, we report the formation of an unusual M12L4L′4 cage (MCC) with double-walled knotted architecture via multicomponent self-assembly of a tripyridyl ligand (L), a tricarboxylate ligand (L′), and a cis-Pd(II) acceptor (M). The structure of the MCC resembles a truncated tetrahedron with two overlaid walls enclosing a distorted cavity. The cavity selectively encapsulates polyaromatic hydrocarbons with two fused rings like naphthalene (G1) and its derivatives [1,4-dibromonaphthalene (G5) and 1,5-dibromonaphthalene (G6)], while it is repellent to larger guests in aqueous media. Interestingly, it shows high selectivity for 1,4-dibromonaphthalene (G5), which enabled the purification of 1,4-dibromonaphthalene and 1,5-dibromonaphthalene (G6) from their mixture in aqueous media. Furthermore, selective bromination of naphthalene to 1,4-dibromonaphthalene could be achieved within the hydrophobic cavity of MCC in aqueous media under ambient reaction conditions driven by the high specificity of the cavity for G5, while the same bromination in the absence of the cage yields a mixture of dibromo and monobromo derivatives. Thus, the newly designed cage (MCC) could be utilized for developing an efficient strategy for the regioselective bromination of naphthalene, overcoming the challenges associated with separating the product mixture generated in conventional bromination. Moreover, the cage enables efficient separation of the dibromo isomers of naphthalene formed in conventional synthesis.

title: Ligand Curvature Controls the Size of Self-Assembled Twisted Metallacycles
abstract: Abstract Coordination-driven self-assembly often yields dynamic libraries of metallacycles whose size distribution is difficult to control, and ligand-design strategies for directing such equilibria have so far been limited to discrete changes in coordination angles. Here we introduce the first twisted metallacycles, in which ligand curvature is tuned through the tether-to-twist approach. Two twistacene dipyridyl ligands with only a 6° difference in the overall bend: the nearly planar Pl (14° twist) and the twisted Tw (34° twist) assemble with (dppp)Pd(II) and (dppp)Pt(II) corners {M} into dynamic equilibria between rhomboidal {M}2L2 and hexagonal {M}3L3 metallacycles. NMR, nanoESI-MS and X-ray crystallography show that racemic ligands self-sort with high fidelity: socially, into heterochiral meso {M}2L2 rhomboids, and narcissistically, into homochiral {M}3L3 hexagons. Van ‘t Hoff analysis shows ring expansion to be endothermic and entropy-driven throughout, with an enthalpic cost rising from 6–10 kJ mol–1 for Pl to 17–18 kJ mol–1 for Tw. This is explained by increased strain energy for mismatched planar ligands in {M}2L2 assemblies. A few degrees of backbone curvature therefore reshape the free-energy landscape of coordination-driven self-assembly.

title: Intrinsic Catalyst Reactivity—not Matched Surfactant Polarity—Drives Yield Differences in Aqueous Cross‐Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT Micelles in aqueous–organic syntheses are commonly assumed to be the primary reaction sites that colocalize and transform reactants. However, under synthetically relevant high‐concentration conditions, including those used at scale in industrial pharmaceutical synthesis, phase separation may alter this simplified picture in poorly understood ways. Here, we investigate an aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura cross‐coupling producing a fluorescent product using triethylamine base and Kolliphor EL or Tween 80 surfactants. Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM), dual‐channel imaging, and microspectroscopy reveal that micrometer‐scale triethylamine‐rich organic droplets, rather than nanoscale surfactant micelles, function as the predominant reaction sites. Direct measurements of droplet and micelle molecular compositions disprove a proposed product‐saturation inhibition mechanism based on surfactant polarity matching. Instead, the observed yield differences arise primarily from intrinsic catalyst reactivity. Surfactant‐free “on‐water” reactions further show that micelles are not required for productive coupling, supporting a primary role for surfactant in homogenization and mass transfer rather than creation of selective reaction compartments. This revised mechanistic assignment redirected reaction optimization from surfactant polarity to catalyst reactivity, affording 95% conversion to product in 20 min versus 26% under prior conditions. These findings challenge prevailing assumptions regarding micellar catalysis and demonstrate how microscale imaging can enable predictive optimization of aqueous reactions.

title: Spontaneous Emulsification of Long‐Chain Alkanes to Form Oil‐in‐Water Nano‐Emulsions
abstract: ABSTRACT Spontaneous emulsification (SE) of long‐chain alkanes (LCA) to form oil‐in‐water (O/W) emulsion (SE‐O/W‐LCA) holds significant promise for applications such as oil sands extraction. However, SE‐O/W‐LCA remains a long‐standing challenge due to the extremely low polarity of LCA and high oil‐water interfacial tension. Herein, we present a successful strategy for achieving SE‐O/W‐LCA based on the design of surfactant molecular architecture. Systematic studies on structure–activity relationship correlating the structure of surfactant molecular segments with SE performance lead to an optimized surfactant architecture that achieves an emulsification capacity approximately two orders of magnitude higher than that of conventional surfactants. A general design guideline of surfactants is established, requiring both high LCA solubility and large hydrophilic–lipophilic balance (HLB) values for efficient SE. Fundamentally, the integrated SE mechanism, involving reverse‐micelle diffusion, Marangoni‐flow and O/W droplet formation, is elucidated alongside the corresponding thermodynamic basis and kinetic evolution. Finally, the developed strategy is successfully applied to practical oil sands extraction that delivers state‐of‐the‐art oil‐solid separation performance as compared with previously reported methods. The proposed SE‐O/W‐LCA strategy, together with the understanding of surfactant design guidelines and underlying mechanisms, is anticipated to inspire future research on low‐energy emulsification and advance the widespread industrial deployment of SE technology.

title: Biomass-enabled metal−organic framework-based macroarchitectural materials with advanced applications
abstract: Purpose The rising global demand for energy, together with the environmental pressures linked to industrial growth, has made sustainable green development a global priority. This review focuses on biomass-enabled MOF macroarchitectures as an important class of sustainable porous materials. Design/methodology/approach This review focuses on three main aspects: fabrication strategies, structure–property relationships (dimensions) and advanced applications. It covers key synthesis routes such as templating, interfacial assembly and reaction confinement, while showing how biomass components such as cellulose, lignin and chitosan influence material formation and performance. The review also explains how pore hierarchy, interface design, surface chemistry, transport pathways and mechanical stability determine the final properties of these systems. Findings By combining the tuneable structure and functionality of MOFs with the renewability, hierarchical architecture and easy processability of biomass, these materials address major drawbacks of conventional MOF powders, especially poor shape control, weak mechanical strength, limited mass transfer and difficult device integration. Their growing applications in adsorption, catalysis, environmental cleanup, energy storage and drug delivery are highlighted. Current challenges include large-scale production, interface control, durability and limited mechanistic understanding. Originality/value The article points to future directions for designing application-oriented biomass-enabled MOF macroarchitectures. These materials are expected to become a key platform for scalable and high-performance next-generation technologies.

title: Amine Vapor Activated Superior Proton Conduction in a Barium Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) show promise as solid electrolytes for proton exchange membrane fuel cells, yet progress is hindered by a limited number of proton-conductive materials and an incomplete understanding of the underlying mechanisms. This study presents a 3D barium-based MOF, {[Ba(p-CPhH2IDC)(H2O)2]}n (Ba-MOF-1), synthesized using 2-(4-carboxyphenyl)-1H-imidazole-4,5-dicarboxylic acid. Its structure features abundant unprotonated carboxyl oxygens, imidazole nitrogens, and coordinated water, creating a favorable environment for proton transport. While Ba-MOF-1 exhibits modest proton conductivity under humid conditions (1.13 × 10–5 S·cm–1 at 98% RH and 100 °C), its performance is dramatically enhanced upon exposure to volatile bases. At 100 °C in 2 M ammonia vapor, conductivity surges to 5.26 × 10–3 S·cm–1-a 465-fold increase. Similarly, at 70 °C, vapors from 2 M methylamine, dimethylamine, and ethylamine solutions boost conductivity by factors of 367, 299, and 230, respectively, compared to humid conditions alone. This enhancement is attributed to the adsorption of basic molecules within the MOF’s pores, where they act both as additional proton carriers and as direct proton sources, synergistically facilitating proton conduction.

title: Hydrothermal Synthesis of Porous MoS<sub>2</sub> Nanosheets for Aqueous Electrochemical Capacitors<b></b>
abstract: Porous MoS2 nanosheets were synthesized by a hydrothermal method and investigated as electrode materials for aqueous supercapacitors. X-ray diffraction confirmed the formation of crystalline hexagonal MoS2 with an average crystallite size of approximately 3.12 nm. Scanning electron microscopy revealed a three-dimensional marigold-like assembly of interlinked nanosheets. Nitrogen adsorption-desorption measurements indicated a mesoporous textural structure, with a BET surface area of 4.6962 m2 g-1, total pore volume of 0.03011 cm3 g-1, and average pore width of approximately 25.8 nm. The high-relative-pressure hysteresis is consistent with interparticle voids within the nanosheet assembly. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy confirmed the presence of Mo and S, with no impurity-related elemental signals detected within the measurement sensitivity. Electrochemical performance was evaluated in 1 M KOH using a three-electrode system. Cyclic voltammetry showed Faradaic charge-storage behavior and delivered a specific capacitance of 165.17 F g-1 at a scan rate of 10 mV s-1. Galvanostatic charge-discharge measurements yielded a specific capacitance of 110.66 F g-1 at 1 A g-1, corresponding to estimated electrode-level gravimetric energy and power densities of 7.53 Wh kg-1 and 349.95 W kg-1, respectively. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed electrolyte and charge-transfer resistances of 4.75 and 1.77 Ω, respectively, indicating favorable ion transport and charge-transfer kinetics. Kinetic analysis indicated a mixed charge-storage mechanism dominated by diffusion-controlled processes, with a smaller surface-controlled contribution. The mesoporous nanosheet assembly, together with the observed electrochemical performance, demonstrates the potential of hydrothermally prepared MoS2 as an electrode material for aqueous supercapacitors.

title: Injectable Self‐Healing Microspheres Enable In Situ Assembly of Dynamic Porous Scaffolds for Tissue Repair
abstract: ABSTRACT Tissue engineering scaffolds are indispensable for repairing complex tissue defects; however, conventional prefabricated scaffolds are limited by invasive implantation, poor anatomical conformity, and insufficient adaptability to irregular defect geometries. Here, we report an injectable, self‐assembling scaffold strategy that transforms polymer microspheres from isolated functional carriers into dynamic modular building blocks for in situ scaffold construction. Following injection, the self‐healing microspheres fill irregular defects, fuse with adjacent microspheres, and form a mechanically stable three‐dimensional scaffold with an interconnected porous architecture. This design combines the minimally invasive delivery and functional versatility of microspheres with the structural integrity and mechanical support of macroscopic scaffolds, thereby addressing a key challenge in precise and conformal tissue repair. The platform also enables disease‐specific functionalization through metal‐ion coordination. Silver‐ion‐loaded microspheres provide conformal coverage of complex wounds while exhibiting antibacterial activity and supporting skin regeneration. Zinc‐ion‐functionalized microspheres assemble into defect‐matched porous scaffolds and promote osteogenic repair. Copper‐ion‐integrated microspheres remain localized at tumor sites and provide sustained release of therapeutic agents, thereby reducing systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work establishes a minimally invasive, shape‐adaptive, and customizable scaffold platform for complex tissue repair and localized therapy. More broadly, it provides a versatile design framework for the development of next‐generation intelligent biomaterials.

title: A Cryptic Cytochrome P450 Radical Cyclase Catalyzes Naphthalene-Ring Closure in Rifamycin Biosynthesis
abstract: Abstract The enzymatic assembly of the 8-hydroxynaphthalene chromophore in rifamycins presents a classic biosynthetic paradox: the off-PKS precursor, prorifamycin A (1a), readily suffers nonenzymatic deoxygenative collapse in solution into the aberrant product 8-deoxynaphthoquinones. Here, using in cellulo genetic manipulation, stepwise pathway reconstitution, in vitro enzymatic assays, molecular docking, and DFT calculations, we identified Rif-Orf0 to be a cytochrome P450 radical cyclase. Rif-Orf0 converted 1a to the 8-hydroxy-7,8-dihydronaphthalenoid intermediate prorifamycin B (1b) through a low-barrier biradical cyclization, and the RifS/RifT dehydrogenase pair rapidly captured and oxidatively aromatized 1b to 34a-deoxyrifamycin W (2). This Rif-Orf0 and RifS/RifT enzymatic cascade outcompeted the spontaneous deoxygenative shunting that afforded 8-deoxynaphthalene-type rifamycins, thereby enforcing the production of 8-hydroxynaphthalenoid rifamycins. This study expanded the catalytic repertoire of cytochrome P450 enzymes and resolved a long-standing question in rifamycin biosynthesis by characterizing how tailoring enzymes canalized reactive intermediates from spontaneous reactions toward defined natural product architectures.

title: Highly Crystalline Triptycene-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Achieving high crystallinity in three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains a fundamental challenge, particularly beyond 4-connected tetrahedral nodes toward higher-connectivity building units. Here, we report the rapid synthesis of three highly crystalline triptycene-based COFs (COF-563, −564, and −565) as well-faceted, micrometer-sized crystals under mild conditions within 24 h. By employing rigid 6-connected trigonal prismatic triptycene-based building units, hexakis(4-aminophenyl/4-formylphenyl)triptycene (Trip-NH2/Trip-CHO), we access a topological regime of three-dimensional (3D) COFs that includes the established hea and stp nets as well as an unprecedented (6,6)-connected htp topology. These frameworks are constructed through reticulation of the triptycene nodes with tetrahedral (tetra(4-anilyl)methane (TAM)), rectangular (pyrene-1,3,6,8-tetraaniline (PyTTA)), and hexagonal (hexakis(4′-formyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)benzene (HFBB)) complementary linkers to yield the hea, stp, and htp structures, respectively. The resulting materials exhibit permanent porosity with Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface areas of up to 3769 m2 g–1─approaching a 2-fold increase over previously reported values for related topologies─and thermal stability up to 500 °C. This work establishes a versatile platform for the rapid formation of highly crystalline 3D organic frameworks and provides a blueprint for designing complex, highly porous architectures with controlled topology.

title: Solvent‐Induced Reversible Phase Transition in Microporous Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Frameworks for Molecular‐Sieving Separation of CO 2 and C 2 H 2
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient separation of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from acetylene (C 2 H 2 ) remains a critical challenge in the chemical industry for C 2 H 2 purification, due to their highly similar molecular sizes and physicochemical property. Here we report a HOF material, denoted HIAM‐105, assembled from a tetracarboxylic acid building block. It undergoes reversible structural transformation upon solvent removal and inclusion. The guest‐free structure (HIAM‐105a) features precisely matched pore dimensions with CO 2 molecules while fully excluding C 2 H 2 , enabling molecular sieving separation of CO 2 /C 2 H 2 . At 298 K and 1 bar, HIAM‐105a achieves a CO 2 adsorption capacity of 44.0 cm 3 g −1 , resulting in a CO 2 /C 2 H 2 adsorption capacity ratio as high as 23.9, which outperforms most previously reported sieving adsorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm that HIAM‐105a can produce C 2 H 2 with ultrahigh purity from CO 2 /C 2 H 2 mixtures, and more importantly, it can be readily regenerated through gas purging at ambient conditions.

title: Synergistic Coordination and Crosslinking Strategy for Scalable, Self‐Repairable C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 Separation Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT Ethylene/ethane (C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 ) separation is one of the most energy‐intensive processes in the chemical industry, and membrane technology offers a promising low‐energy alternative. However, conventional mixed‐matrix membranes (MMMs) suffer from poor filler dispersion and interfacial defects, especially at high MOF loadings. Here we report a synergistic coordination and crosslinking strategy to fabricate highly compatible, high‐loaded UTSA‐280‐integrated hydrogel MMMs for efficient C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 separation. By exploiting the dual role of calcium ions (Ca 2+ ), which simultaneously coordinate with squaric acid to grow UTSA‐280 and crosslink sodium alginate (SA) chains, we achieve in situ growth of uniformly dispersed UTSA‐280 nanoparticles (mean size 4.32 nm) within a semisolid hydrogel network. The resulting membrane exhibits a high MOF loading of 27.39 wt%, a C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 mixture separation factor of 4.0 at 7 bar, and stable operation for over 1780 h. The hydrogel matrix also confers a remarkable self‐repair capability, fully restoring separation performance after mechanical damage. Moreover, a 200 cm 2 large‐area membrane was readily fabricated, demonstrating a cost‐effective route to scalable ethylene purification.

title: Engineered Pore Bisection by a Cymbal‐Shaped Cycloaliphatic Pillar in a Zn‐Triazolate Metal–Organic Framework (MOF) for Selective CO 2 Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT Physisorbents combining ultramicroporosity, high CO 2 affinity, and humidity tolerance remain a challenge in carbon‐capture materials. MOFs based on flexible Zn‐triazolate layers have emerged as a promising platform; however, balancing pore size, confinement, and regeneration remains nontrivial. Here we introduce a new pillared‐layer MOF, ZnTzBCP, constructed from Zn 2 + cations, 1,2,4‐triazolate (Tz) linkers, and the 3‐dimensional cycloaliphatic bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane‐1,3‐dicarboxylate (BCP) linker. Liquid‐assisted mechanochemical grinding affords a crystalline material in which the rigid BCP pillars with a cymbal‐shaped core bisect the pore space into symmetric twin ultramicropores with dimensions commensurate with the CO 2 kinetic diameter. Combined PXRD/PW‐DFT/Rietveld analysis integrated with gas sorption, calorimetry, and CO 2 ‐loaded structural refinement reveals reversible, guest‐responsive flexibility of the Zn‐Tz layers through anisotropic swelling of the MOF with CO 2 molecules generating multiple cooperative C─H···O interactions with both ligands and yielding high adsorption enthalpies of 41 kJ/mol. These properties are retained in a PVDF composite, which demonstrates stable, cyclic CO 2 capture under humid breakthrough conditions with minimal thermal regeneration (333 K) and outstanding selectivity for CO 2 over nitrogen of 226. These findings position the linkers with a cymbal‐shaped core as powerful pore‐controlling elements for the design of ultramicroporous MOFs capable of selective CO 2 capture under operative conditions.

title: Hydroxamate Reticular Chemistry beyond Metals: Single-Crystalline Two- and Three-Dimensional Boron–Hydroxamate Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Hydroxamate chelation has already enabled robust metal–organic frameworks. Here, to move the corresponding reticular chemistry beyond metal nodes, hydroxamate chelation has been integrated within heteroleptic tetracoordinate B(O,O)(N)(C) centers to construct four single-crystalline boron–hydroxamate covalent organic frameworks, namely SUM-306–SUM-309. Bayesian optimization enabled the growth of diffraction-quality SUM-306 single crystals, while linker isomerism and functionalization yielded a series spanning two-dimensional hcb and three-dimensional pcu-h frameworks. Structural comparison reveals extended anti-B–phenylene–B arrangements in SUM-306 and SUM-307 and folded syn arrangements in SUM-308 and SUM-309, associated with their respective two- and three-dimensional propagation. Solid-state NMR spectroscopy, B K-edge XANES, and electronic-structure calculations support tetracoordinate boron formation and differentiated yet substantial bonding throughout the B(O,O)(N)(C) environment. As a representative of the series, SUM-308 retains accessible microporosity, exhibits a BET surface area of 1279.9 m2 g–1, and preferentially adsorbs and dynamically separates CO2 from N2. These results extend hydroxamate reticular chemistry beyond metals and establish a mixed-linkage strategy combining chelation, donor–acceptor coordination, and covalent anchoring for single-crystalline boron-based framework construction.

title: [8+4]‐Connected Ether‐Oxygen‐Based 3D COF Redox Mediators for Durable Light‐Assisted Indirect Electrocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Ether‐oxygen is a type of functional group with high chemical stability, electronic modulation capability, and imparted molecular flexibility, yet incorporating ether‐oxygen groups into high‐connectivity covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to explore their extended applications remains a challenge. Herein, we have designed a series of [8+4]‐connected 3D COFs with scu topology, named TADM–TAPP–COF(M) (M = Ni, Mn, and Cu), by introducing eight‐connected ether‐oxygen based building blocks and metalloporphyrin nodes, which can be applied in high‐stability light‐assisted indirect electrocatalysis. These 3D COFs exhibit good crystallinity, nanosheet morphology, flexible 3D pore structure, abundant ether‐oxygen groups and active metal sites, and excellent electrolyte affinity, which can act as efficient redox mediators. Impressively, the Ni‐incorporated structure TADM–TAPP–COF (Ni) demonstrates high yield in the condensation cyclization reaction of aromatic aldehydes and 2‐aminobenzenethiol to produce 2‐phenylbenzothiazole (yields up to 96%), coupled with the simultaneous production of gas‐phase H 2 product (∼1.15 mmol g −1 h −1 ). Notably, it also shows remarkable stability (continuous reaction for 300 h), high recyclability (8 cycles), and scale‐up production ability (about 2 g in a 12 h batch experiment) and wide substrate applicability, providing a valuable example for the structural design of catalysts toward light‐assisted indirect electrocatalysis.

title: Guest-Modulated Pyrene-Based Metal–Organic Framework toward Enhanced Photocatalytic H2 Evolution
abstract: Abstract The development of efficient photocatalysts for solar-driven H2 production remains a challenge in sustainable energy research. Herein, we report a guest-modulated strategy to construct a high-performance photocatalyst by encapsulating a cationic dye, (4-dimethylaminostyryl)-1-methylpyridine (DMASM), into an anionic pyrene-based metal–organic framework (MOF), Zn-Py ([BMI]3[Na3Zn3(TBAPy)3], H4TBAPy = 1,3,6,8-tetrakis(p-benzoic acid)pyrene), synthesized via ionic liquid-directed assembly. The resulting host–guest system, DMASM@Zn-Py, exhibits a narrowed bandgap from 2.39 to 2.02 eV, significantly extending visible-light absorption. Spectroscopic investigations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal efficient energy transfer from the TBAPy ligand to the DMASM guest, accompanied by spatial separation of the highest occupied crystal orbital (HOCO) and lowest unoccupied crystal orbital (LUCO) on the framework and dye, respectively. This spatial separation effectively suppresses photogenerated electron–hole recombination, as evidenced by about a 5.6-fold enhancement in photocurrent density and a substantially reduced charge-transfer resistance. Remarkably, DMASM@Zn-Py achieves a cocatalyst-free photocatalytic H2 evolution rate of 1065.5 μmol·g–1·h–1, far surpassing that of pristine Zn-Py (225.69 μmol·g–1·h–1). This work establishes a clear molecular engineering paradigm for designing efficient MOF-based photocatalysts through tunable host–guest interactions.

title: Surface-Driven Assembly of Bent-Core Liquid Crystals on HOPG: Insights into Kinetic and Thermodynamic Control from STM and Quantum Mechanical Simulations
abstract: The self-assembly of bent-core liquid crystals (BCLC) is critical for understanding and controlling interfacial ordering in functional soft materials. Here, we investigate the adsorption and 2D self-assembly of an azobenzene-containing BCLC molecule, AzB-BC, at the 1,2,4-trichlorobenzene/highly ordered pyrolytic graphite (HOPG(0001)) interface using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations. STM imaging reveals the spontaneous formation of extended lamellar monolayers characterized by bright aromatic bands separated by head-to-head alkyl chains, with the emergence of multiple chiral domains at room temperature. Ex situ thermal annealing leads to a single-domain monolayer, indicating a transition from kinetically trapped assemblies to a thermodynamically favored configuration. STM image-guided periodic DFT calculations identify two low energy molecular conformations differing in the orientation of the terminal alkoxy chains, with similar adsorption energies on HOPG. The calculations show that π–π interactions between the aromatic bent-core units and the HOPG surface drive the surface orientation of the BCLC molecule, while alkyl chains primarily govern lateral packing through van der Waals interactions. Together, the combined experimental and theoretical results provide the first detailed insight into the adsorption energetics and conformational preferences of a bent-core liquid crystal on an ordered graphitic surface, offering a molecular-level framework for designing surface-confined liquid crystal systems.

title: Conjugation Relay Beyond Local Coordination Rebalances Oxygen Intermediate Binding at Paired Cobalt Sites
abstract: Abstract Correlated adsorption of oxygenated intermediates at single-metal sites limits the independent regulation of elementary steps in the oxygen reduction reaction. Herein, we establish a conjugation relay that tunes a structurally conserved cobalt pair through its molecular framework and carbon interface. We construct a pyrolysis-free series comprising a dicobalt complex and two conjugated coordination polymers grown directly on Ketjen Black, progressively extending the π network while retaining comparable Co2N4O2 pockets and cobalt loadings. Microscopy and X-ray absorption spectroscopy support comparable cobalt pairing and local coordination across the series. Comparisons with unsupported counterparts and a physical mixture help distinguish molecular conjugation, direct interfacial coupling, and conductive contact. Spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations show that molecular π extension redistributes charge around the cobalt pair and that carbon coupling amplifies this response. Within the paired pocket, *OOH spans both cobalt centers, whereas *OH remains bound primarily to one center. These distinct geometries cause their adsorption free energies to respond unequally, decreasing the ΔG*OOH – ΔG*OH offset from the 3.13 eV single-site reference to 2.62 eV for the most conjugated supported model. Potential-dependent infrared spectroscopy detects *OOH at more positive potentials as conjugation increases, supporting facilitated formation under reaction conditions. The most conjugated catalyst delivers an iR-corrected half-wave potential of 1.02 V, with only a 13 mV loss after 30,000 cycles. These findings establish conjugation beyond local coordination as a molecular design strategy for relaxing adsorption-energy correlations at multiatom catalytic sites.

title: Metal–Backboned Architectures Enable Magneto–Spin–Charge Engineering for High–Performance Li–CO 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Simultaneous CO 2 conversion and high–energy–density energy storage are urgently needed for sustainable energy systems where Li–CO 2 batteries provide an ideal solution, yet their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish CO 2 redox kinetics. Emerging metal–backboned molecules, which contain numerous metal atoms as catalytically active sites, are expected to accelerate CO 2 reduction reaction kinetics due to their unique architectures and properties. Herein, we report a novel mixed–valence cobalt–backboned polymer with effective spin manipulation as an efficient electrocatalyst and conductive scaffold for Li–CO 2 batteries, which enables a low overpotential of 1.06 V and outstanding stable cycling over 2700 h. An external magnetic field drives Co centers from low–spin to high–spin configuration and enhances intermetallic intervalence charge transfer, synergistically strengthening CO 2 adsorption and activation by increasing unpaired electron orbital occupancy and facilitating electron transfer to CO 2 antibonding orbitals. This work establishes metal–backboned architectures as a versatile platform for spin–charge cooperative engineering, opening a new avenue for kinetically accelerated next–generation energy storage systems.

title: Fully π‐Conjugated Nonvolatile n‐Type Additives Toward 21% Efficiency in Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid additive engineering represents a key strategy to modulate the morphology of organic solar cells via intermolecular interactions (van der Waals forces, hydrogen bonds, and dipole interaction) with photoactive materials. However, these weak interactions lack sufficient capacity to control the crystallization and phase separation of active layer. Here, we developed a conjugated electrostatic coupling strategy to strengthen the intermolecular forces between solid additives and donor/acceptor. The solid additive we designed possesses a fully conjugated structure that can generate strong electrostatic potential interaction, therefore a small amount of solid additive (3 wt%) facilitate ordered crystalline fibril growth of polymer donor and dense molecular packing of acceptor. In addition, the n‐type nature and nonvolatile feature of solid additive promotes the electron transport capacity and stability of the active layer. As a result, the optimal device achieved a state‐of‐the‐art efficiency of 21.02% (certificated to 20.55%), due to the prolonged exciton lifetime, suppressed charge recombination, and enhanced charge collection efficiency. This work establishes a new paradigm for solid additive engineering in organic photovoltaics.

title: Dual‐Asymmetric Giant Molecule Acceptors Featuring Asymmetric Terminals and Flexible Alkyl‐Flank Architecture for Efficient and Robust Non‐Halogen Solvent‐Processed Binary and Ternary Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible‐linked giant‐molecule acceptors (F‐GMAs) suffer from inferior intermolecular packing, limiting their efficiency in non‐halogenated processed binary organic solar cells (OSCs). Moreover, asymmetric‐terminal‐based regioregular F‐GMAs remain challenging. Here, we propose a dual‐asymmetric‐rigid‐within‐flexible molecular strategy and synthesize four flanking linker‐based F‐GMAs ( DY4T‐F , DY8T‐F , DY12T‐F , dual‐asymmetric ADY8T‐FCl ) by progressively lengthening the alkyl linker and symmetric/asymmetric terminals, alongside a dual‐asymmetric monomeric AY4T‐FCl . The AY4T‐FCl crystal exhibited diverse intermolecular packing modes and efficient charge transport channels due to the synergistic outer thienyl flanking chain and asymmetric terminals. ADY8T‐FCl exhibits stronger intramolecular folding, enhanced crystallinity, and higher electron mobility than other neat films. o ‐XY: CS 2 ‐processed D18 : ADY8T‐FCl ‐based as‐cast binary OSCs yield a remarkable PCE of 20.35% with a low nonradiative recombination energy loss (Δ E 3 ) of 0.183 eV, setting benchmarks for all‐F‐GMA‐based and non‐halogenated‐solvent‐processed binary OSCs. Notably, D18 : ADY8T‐FCl flexible binary OSCs achieve an outstanding PCE of 18.41%, significantly better than other counterparts. More interestingly, D18 : L8‐BO‐X : ADY8T‐FCl ‐based devices achieve a champion PCE of 20.82% among F‐GMAs‐based ternary OSCs. Our work demonstrates that the dual‐asymmetric‐rigid‐within‐flexible strategy for flank‐connected F‐GMAs with alkyl‐length engineering and asymmetric terminals offers a promising pathway for concurrently achieving record efficiency, ultralow Δ E 3 , and superior mechanical robustness in non‐halogenated processed flexible/rigid binary and rigid ternary OSCs.

title: Steric Effect of Branch Grafting Enables Highly Soluble and Stable Phenazines in Aqueous Organic Flow Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Phenazine‐based derivatives demonstrated promising potential in aqueous organic flow batteries (AOFBs) due to their features of low redox potential and the capability to undergo a one‐step two‐electron redox reaction. However, the highly conjugated structure of phenazine reduces molecular polarity and limits the solubility in electrolytes. Herein, we introduced a branched chain to achieve a highly stable and soluble phenazine derivative for AOFBs. The branched structure can effectively suppress the π – π interaction of the phenazine conjugation system but also inhibit the hydrolysis of the ether bond by steric hindrance, which significantly enhances the structural stability. The AOFB using a 1.0 mol/L electrolyte of 2,2′‐(phenazine‐2,3‐diylbis(oxy))dipropionic acid exhibited a high discharge capacity of 45.5 Ah/L and a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.00017% per cycle, with stable operation for more than 42 days (1200 cycles). Furthermore, a pilot‐scale stack demonstrated excellent cycling stability, with negligible capacity degradation after 400 cycles. The outstanding AOFB performance suggests its promise for large‐scale energy storage applications.

title: Heat‐Activated Reversible Conjugation Switching in Polymers Through Cooperative Ion Pairing
abstract: Thermochromic conjugated polymers generally undergo transitions from colored to less‐colored states upon heating due to disruption of π‐conjugation. In contrast, heat‐triggered switching from a colorless state to a more intensely colored conjugated state remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a reversible conjugation‐switching polymer system governed by cooperative interactions between metal cations and counteranions. By incorporating lactone‐functionalized xanthene units directly into conjugated polymer backbones, weakly solvated Li + , Na + , and Ag + ions, acting cooperatively with their weakly coordinating counteranions, induce lactone ring opening and establish linear conjugation along the polymer backbone, thereby producing pronounced optical responses. Coordination of the metal ions by isopropanol reverses the process and restores the colorless state. A series of conjugated copolymers displayed thermally activated multicolor responses spanning blue, green, yellow, orange, red, magenta, and black, enabling rewritable invisible‐ink systems on paper substrates. Density functional theory calculations support a nearly barrierless Li + /PF 6 − ion‐pair‐cooperation‐promoted ring‐opening process and reveal reversible switching between twisted nonconjugated and planar linearly conjugated states. These results establish a metal‐ion‐regulated conjugation‐switching strategy for heat‐activated colorless‐to‐colored switching and responsive optical materials.

title: Dual‐Force Strategy for Universal Clusteroluminescence in Non‐Conjugated Small Molecules
abstract: ABSTRACT Non‐traditional luminophores (NTLs) without extended π‐conjugation are attractive for bio‐applications, yet an effective strategy to impart bright emission to non‐luminescent small molecules remains challenging. In this work, we report a modular strategy based on the diethylenetriamine (DETA)‐induced universal luminescence (DIUL) effect, which converts simple non‐conjugated precursors into highly emissive cluster‐based small molecules via synergistic dual‐force: ionic (─BF 4 − /─NH 2 + ) and hydrogen‐bonding (─NH─/─NH 2 ) interactions. The resulting seven derivatives exhibit >70% photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) in water, with emission independent of ring/chain structure, demonstrating a robust dual‐force mechanism that advances beyond hydrogen‐bond‐dominated aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) models. These probes show excellent water solubility, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling high‐contrast dual‐color cellular and deep 3D tumor spheroid imaging, along with long‐term biocompatible zebrafish imaging. This work establishes a versatile modular functionalization platform for bright NTLs, offering fundamental insights into cooperative non‐covalent interactions and opening new avenues for designing multifunctional optical materials in bioimaging, sensing, and encryption.

title: Single‐Atom Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption Enables Ultrafast Charge Transfer for Boosting Photocatalytic H 2 Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐atom cocatalysts with near‐100% atom utilization are widely studied for boosting photocatalytic H 2 evolution, but their mechanistic insights remain largely restricted to idealized mono‐hydrogen adsorption models. Such simplified frameworks fail to capture the complexity of operando reaction environments, where the high coordination unsaturation of single atoms inevitably drives a transition toward multi‐hydrogen adsorption states. Here, we demonstrate that an N‐coordinated Ni single‐atom cocatalyst (Ni SA ‐N) forms a multi‐hydrogen adsorption state during actual photocatalytic H 2 evolution, significantly accelerating ultrafast charge transfer kinetics. Research results demonstrate that the adsorption of multiple hydrogen triggers spontaneous free‐electron delocalization, rendering the Ni center into a unique electron‐deficient (δ + ) feature. This dynamic electronic reconfiguration enhances the interfacial d‐p orbital hybridization between Ni SA and S of CdS, effectively shortening the interfacial Ni–S bond to construct a highly conductive channel that facilitates ultrafast electron transfer from the CdS to Ni SA cocatalyst, as elucidated by femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy. Consequently, the Ni SA ‐N/CdS system achieves an exceptional H 2 evolution rate of 20.20 mmol h −1 g −1 . This work identifies the multi‐hydrogen adsorption state as a pivotal nexus linking surface chemistry to ultrafast dynamics, providing a conceptual framework for engineering high‐performance catalysts for artificial photosynthesis.

title: Coupling Iodine Regulation With Hole‐Selective Interfaces for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Operational instability remains a major barrier to the practical application of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), where the formation and volatilization of molecular iodine (I 2 ) cause irreversible degradation of both the perovskite and adjacent hole‐transport layer (HTL). Existing iodine‐trapping or reducing agents can mitigate this degradation, but often compromise interfacial charge transport. Here, we develop two amidinium‐based interfacial modifiers, PTZ‐PEFAI and PXZ‐PEFAI, that combine iodine regulation, favorable energy‐level alignment, and defect passivation. Density functional theory calculations and experiments show that the S/O sites of phenothiazine (PTZ) and phenoxazine (PXZ) interact with I 2 through halogen bonding, enabling I 2 capture and dissociation. The direct identification of I 3 − in modifier‐iodine cocrystals further supports the regeneration of iodide ions. At the perovskite surface, these interactions suppress iodine loss, replenish iodide, and promote healing of iodine‐vacancy defects. Meanwhile, the p‐type PTZ/PXZ functionalities improve energy‐level alignment and facilitate hole extraction at the perovskite/HTL interface. Consequently, PTZ‐PEFAI‐treated n–i–p PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.34% and a T 85 lifetime exceeding 1500 h under maximum‐power‐point tracking at 65°C. This work provides a molecular design strategy for simultaneously regulating interfacial iodine chemistry and charge transport toward efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Matcha-Assisted Synthesis of a NiCo2O4−ZnO-rGO Ternary Nanoarchitecture for Nanomolar Level Electrochemical Dopamine Detection
abstract: Abstract Developing cost-effective, environmentally benign and highly sensitive electrocatalysts for neurochemical sensing remains a crucial goal in bioanalytical chemistry. Herein, we report a green, hydrothermal strategy for synthesizing a NiCo2O4−ZnO-reduced graphene oxide (rGO) ternary nanoarchitecture using matcha green tea extract as a multifunctional stabilizing and reducing agent. The bioactive phytochemicals in matcha mediated the simultaneous nucleation of redox-active NiCo2O4, ZnO nanoparticles alongside the partial reduction of graphene oxide, forming an interconnected conductive network without toxic chemical reductants. Structural and morphological characterizations confirmed the successful integration of all three functional phases. Electrochemical assessments via cyclic voltammetry (CV) revealed that the NiCo2O4−ZnO-rGO exhibited the highest oxidation peak current of 6.24 μA, compared with 1.13 μA for bare GCE and around 3−5 μA for individual and binary modified electrodes, displaying a superior electrocatalytic oxidation current for dopamine (DA) driven by synergistic charge transfer between the multi-valence transition metals and the highly conductive rGO framework. Chronoamperometric analysis demonstrated a broad working range of 0.02−300 μM, comprising three linear regions of 0.02−0.10, 0.20−8, and 10−300 μM. The low-concentration region exhibited the highest sensitivity of 8.409 μA cm-2 μM-1 with an LOD of 8.9 nM. CV calibration showed two linear regions of 2−8 and 10−100 μM, with an LOD of 71 nM determined from the low-concentration region. Furthermore, the sensor demonstrates excellent anti-interference capabilities in the simultaneous presence of uric acid, ascorbic acid and glucose, alongside robust reproducibility, repeatability and operational stability. This work establishes a sustainable, facile synthesis route for high-performance non-precious nanomaterials in clinical and neurochemical diagnostic applications.

title: Self‐Templated Catalytic Assembly Overcomes Diffusion Limits in Dynamic DNA Circuits for Sensitive Biomarker Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic DNA circuits offer programmable platforms for clinical biomarker detection, but their translation is limited by slow diffusion‐controlled kinetics and inadequate amplification of low‐abundance targets. Herein, we introduce a self‐templated catalytic assembly (SCA) circuit that overcomes diffusion limitations by converting target‐induced catalytic assembly into an amplified fluorescence signal, enabling robust and efficient detection of N‐terminal pro‐brain natriuretic peptide (NT‐proBNP), the gold‐standard biomarker for heart failure (HF). The SCA circuit employs interconnected hairpin reactants that autonomously assemble into a dynamic four‐branched DNA scaffold, which spatially concentrates probes and converts diffusion‐limited hybridization into efficient template‐directed catalysis. This design accelerates the reaction rate constant ( k a ) by 2.61‐fold, facilitating repeated catalytic turnover and sustained signal amplification. With aptamer‐guaranteed molecular recognition and localization‐intensified signal amplification, the SCA circuit revealed improved diagnostic performance for HF patients than the clinically adopted fluorescence immunochromatography assay (FICA) in terms of sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic accuracy. Furthermore, the self‐adaptive SCA circuit enabled accurate risk stratification of HF patients, with all samples in the investigated cohort correctly classified. Attributed to the programmability and modularity, the SCA circuit can be readily adapted for detecting trace amounts of clinically relevant biomarkers, providing a pivotal molecular toolbox for real‐time therapeutic monitoring.

title: Desmin filaments extend along actin filaments within the mouse skeletal muscle sarcomere
abstract: Abstract Although desmin intermediate filaments are critical for muscle architecture and homeostasis, their spatial 3D organization remains elusive. Their known localization to sarcomeric Z-lines delimits the periodic array of actin and myosin filaments. Here, using d STORM and SIM sub-diffraction resolution microscopy, we resolve the spatial 3D organization of desmin filaments within mouse skeletal muscle, and reveal they are not confined to Z-lines. Our reconstruction reveals that desmin intermediate filaments extend from Z-lines into the sarcomere interior, where they align with actin filaments. Functional assays show that disrupting desmin filament assembly in normal male mouse muscle using a dominant negative inhibitor of desmin selectively reduces active tension at longer sarcomere lengths, indicating a role for desmin in sarcomere mechanics. These findings expand the structural model of the muscle sarcomere and support a role for desmin in force production.

title: Guiding DNA Double-Crossover-Tile Assembly via Regulating the Growth Pathway
abstract: Double-crossover (DX) tiles are among the earliest and most well-established DNA tile motifs for constructing programmable nanostructures. Many DX-tile assemblies reliably produce micrometer-scale nanotubes that have been widely employed in subsequent studies and applications. Because DX tiles are anisotropic─both in overall geometry and in the arrangement of their constituent DNA duplexes─the resulting nanotubes share a characteristic structural feature: the nanotube axis runs parallel to the tile’s DNA duplexes, while the circumference is oriented perpendicular to them. This preference is attributed to intrinsic curvature that accumulates as tiles join during growth, greater mechanical flexibility of intertile connections perpendicular to the duplexes, or a combination of both effects. Here, we incorporate a single-stranded loop at various positions on a DX tile to investigate whether steric hindrance from the loop can counterbalance this intrinsic curvature, thereby enabling programmable changes in nanotube morphology. Our study reveals a surprising finding: regardless of loop placement position, the resulting nanotubes adopt a geometry in which the DX tile axis is rotated 90° relative to the nanotube axis, and are substantially wider than canonical DX-tile nanotubes. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reveal the underlying assembly pathway: loop-modified DX tiles first polymerize into single-chain tile-string intermediates through preferential axial sticky-end binding, which subsequently coil and close into tile circles or short nanotube segments that seed the growth and elongation of wide nanotubes. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations show that loop-modified DX tiles are conformationally more dynamic than canonical DX tiles, which likely suppresses lateral growth perpendicular to the tile axis and drives tile-string formation. This work expands the morphological diversity of DX tile-based DNA nanotubes and establishes a design strategy for directing tile-array growth through control of hierarchical assembly kinetics.

title: Porphyrin-Phenothiazine-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks for Enhanced Photocatalytic Nitrogen Fixation
abstract: Abstract Solar-driven photocatalytic nitrogen reduction represents a promising and environmentally benign approach for ammonia synthesis. However, developing efficient photocatalysts capable of converting nitrogen to ammonia under ambient conditions remains a significant challenge. Porphyrin compounds exhibit excellent photosensitive properties with strong absorption across both the ultraviolet and visible regions of the solar spectrum, while phenothiazine offers unique optoelectronic activity. In this study, we integrated these two motifs and synthesized a series of novel metal-free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) by structural modification of the phenothiazine linker with a methyl group and with oxygen-containing functional groups. All three frameworks are active for N2 photoreduction under visible light, and the activity depends systematically on the linker: the sulfone-functionalized COF-3 reaches 109.6 ± 3.6 μmol g–1 h–1 (1866.2 ± 60.7 μg h–1 gcat–1), outperforming both the unmodified (COF-1) and the methyl-modified (COF-2) frameworks. Mechanistic analysis and theoretical calculations revealed that the introduced oxygen atoms facilitate the separation and transport of photogenerated electrons within the framework. This work shows that rational molecular-level pre-design and fine-tuning of the linker can profoundly influence the structural and optoelectronic properties of COF-based photocatalysts, enabling superior activity without the need for metallic elements or co-catalysts.

title: Ligand-Engineered Metal–Organic Framework Nanoparticles Link Phase-Selective Localization to Interfacial Reinforcement in Immiscible Polymer Blends
abstract: Abstract Thermodynamic immiscibility and insufficient interfacial adhesion limit the mechanical performance of polymer blends. Although nanoparticles can modify polymer–polymer interfaces, how ligand-dependent surface characteristics relate to phase-selective localization and the accompanying mechanical response remains incompletely understood. Here, a series of ligand-engineered UiO-66 nanoparticles was introduced into polypropylene/polystyrene (PP/PS) blends to compare localization within the PP matrix, the PS dispersed phase, and the PP/PS interfacial region. In the PP/PS blend containing TCPE@UiO-66-NH2/CF3 nanoparticles prepared from an equimolar linker feed, fluorescence is concentrated near the PP/PS interfaces. This blend exhibits pronounced PS-domain refinement and the largest increase in tensile toughness among the formulations examined. At a nanoparticle loading of 1.0 wt %, the tensile toughness increases from 6.6 to 65.5 J cm–3, accompanied by increases in tensile strength and elongation at break. Dual-channel confocal microscopy using MOF-confined and phase-selective aggregation-induced emission probes shows that nanoparticle fluorescence remains associated with PS-rich regions during early tensile loading and that elongated fluorescence features appear during necking. Compared with uncompatibilized PP/PS, the mixed-linker blend shows less pronounced interfacial separation and more extensive drawing of the PP matrix in scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images. Generic coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG-MD) models yield localization trends qualitatively consistent with the microscopy observations and indicate improved stress transfer when hybrid particles localize at the interface. Together, these results correlate ligand-dependent nanoparticle localization with coupled changes in phase morphology, interfacial response, and tensile toughness.

title: Supramolecular Polymeric Ionogels
abstract: Conspectus Polymeric ionogels (PIs), comprising ionic liquids as solvents and swollen polymeric matrices, are expected to play crucial roles in next-generation electronics. Owing to the nearly unlimited diversity of anion–cation combinations, the physicochemical properties of ionogels can be widely tuned. More importantly, in contrast to hydrogels, ionogels inherit the intrinsic ionic conductivity, nonvolatility, and electrochemical stability of ILs, although issues such as higher toxicity and viscosity should be addressed by careful chemical design. To achieve excellent electrical performance and mechanical compliance, the key is to identify suitable motifs for PIs. Reversible physical cross-linking, self-assembly, phase separation, self-healing, and network reorganization are not new in ionic liquids. They have been widely studied in physical ionogels, block copolymer ion gels, poly(ionic liquid)s (PILs), and supramolecular hydrogels. Thus, supramolecular polymeric ionogels (SPIs) are not proposed simply because they contain dynamic cross-links. The main point is to understand how these dynamic junctions work in polymeric ionogels. In other words, we focus on how ionic liquids, polymer chains, and reversible bonds together determine mechanics, conductivity, processability, and device functions. Among several materials, supramolecular polymers are emerging as promising building blocks for designing complex architectures with remarkable properties because of their dynamic and reversible noncovalent interactions. Under deformation, reversible bonds can break to dissipate energy and reassociate to restore the network, which brings self-healability, toughness, recyclability, and stimulus responsiveness. Because ionic liquids (ILs) can interact with polymer chains through many noncovalent forces, the network can be mediated by ion–polymer–bond coupling. According to these structural characteristics, SPIs can be divided into three types: (i) polymeric matrix-mediating supramolecular networks, (ii) IL-mediating supramolecular networks, and (iii) supramolecular networks constructed by both polymeric matrices and ILs. In this Account, we critically summarize recent progress in SPIs based on supramolecular polymers. We initially focus on the chemical design of SPIs and the corresponding supramolecular strategies. Then, we provide insights into the relations between the microscopic chemical design and macroscopic mechanical and electrical properties of SPIs with emphasis on toughness, self-healing, stiffening behavior, low hysteresis, mechanomodulation of ionic conduction, and strain-insensitive ionic conduction enabled by dynamic covalent and noncovalent chemistry. We also discuss processing methods of SPIs, especially 3D printing and fiber spinning. Furthermore, practical applications of SPIs based on their dynamic characteristics are discussed, including adhesives, thermoelectric conversion, electrolytes, and sensors. Finally, we conclude with an outlook on the potential challenges and emerging opportunities in SPIs, including quantitative understanding of how ionic liquid ions compete with or reinforce supramolecular junctions, decoupling of mechanical and ionic relaxation, and long-term electrochemical stability.

title: Engineering Functional Peptide Biomaterials: Self-Assembly, Solid-State Formulation, and Antimicrobial Function
abstract: Peptide-based biomaterials provide precise control over structure, self-assembly, and biological function, making them promising platforms for biomedical applications. However, their translation remains limited by challenges associated with stability, processing, and storage. This review critically examines the relationships between peptide molecular design, supramolecular assembly, polymer interactions, and solid-state engineering, with particular emphasis on how processing and rehydration influence material integrity and biological activity. Four classes of system are distinguished throughout—peptide-structured materials (Class A), peptide–polymer hybrids (Class B), peptide-loaded non-peptidic carriers (Class C), and pharmaceutical protein solids used only as formulation benchmarks (Class D)—because they differ in formation mechanism, critical quality attributes, analytical requirements, and regulatory classification. Drying technologies, particle-based formulations, and route-specific powder design are discussed across pulmonary, nasal, oral, long-acting, transdermal, and wound-applied formats. Functional performance is then analysed specifically for antimicrobial and host-defense peptide materials, while non-antimicrobial functions such as cell adhesion and tissue repair are considered only where they illustrate peptide–polymer integration rather than as separate application classes. Challenges associated with characterization, reproducibility, scale-up, and clinical translation are also addressed. The distinctive contribution of this review is to treat formulation history as a determinant of peptide function rather than as a downstream processing step, and to show that the sequence-level design rules governing assembly were established in solution and remain unvalidated in the dried state, so that solid-state behaviour cannot presently be predicted from sequence design alone.

title: Exploration of Photoclickable Polysaccharide-Gelatin Hydrogels for Vascular Self-Assembly in Three-Dimensional Bioprinted Constructs
abstract: Abstract The future application of extrusion-based bioprinting for human-scale organ engineering requires bioinks that support both extensive vascular development and high shape fidelity during printing. In this study, bioinks based on thiolated gelatin combined with norbornene-modified hyaluronic acid (HANB) or heparin (HepNB), which are photocrosslinkable via thiol-norbornene chemistry, were investigated for their ability to meet these requirements. These hybrid inks, supplemented with unmodified Gelatin-B (Gel-B) and alginate gel porogen (AGP) to improve bioprintability and increase porosity, respectively, form soft (∼5 kPa) hydrogels that support high viability of encapsulated endothelial cells (&gt;70%). Among these formulations, the HANB ink supplemented with both Gel-B and AGP showed the strongest vascular development, supporting vasculogenesis-driven network formation of 22.6 ± 7.5 mm/mm3 and a total angiogenic sprouting length of 4.0 ± 2.3 mm at day 7. Although this ink demonstrated good shape fidelity on a continuous platform, it was unable to consistently bridge gaps larger than 2 mm. In contrast, HANB supplemented with Gel-B alone was able to consistently bridge gaps up to 8 mm while exhibiting reduced vascularization potential compared with its AGP-containing counterpart. To maximize vascular development in bioprinted constructs and maintain the viability of embedded tissues in future applications, the use of HANB with Gel-B and AGP is generally recommended. For complex architectures with overhanging structures, the application of the HANB ink with only Gel-B may be justified, albeit at the cost of reduced vascularization potential.

title: Urea-carbon nanotube composites: Synthesis, characterization, and differential antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli
abstract: This study focuses on the synthesis, characterization, and antibacterial assessment of urea-functionalized carbon nanotube (CNT) composites. Amide nanotubes can be formed through the self-assembly of amphiphilic molecules driven by hydrogen-bonding interactions; however, previously reported approaches may be limited by aggregation and difficulties in large-scale production. In the present work, CNTs were functionalized with urea and systematically characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), thermogravimetric analysis, scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and measurement of the zeta potential to evaluate their structural, chemical, thermal, morphological, and surface-charge properties. The results demonstrated the incorporation of urea-derived functionalities onto the CNT surface. Although functionalization decreased the thermal stability of the CNTs, the spectroscopic results indicated the presence of amide-related functional groups in the CNT–urea–CNT composite. Among the characterization techniques, XPS provided direct evidence of urea incorporation through the appearance of the N 1s signal and corresponding changes in the C 1s and O 1s spectra. Collectively, these results demonstrate substantial modification of the CNT surface following treatment with urea, without implying definitive covalent attachment. Measurement of the zeta potential further revealed a substantial alteration in the surface-charge behavior following functionalization. As pH increased, the zeta potential progressively decreased, a phenomenon that can be attributed to the deprotonation of surface functional groups. Pristine CNTs exhibited an isoelectric point (IEP) at approximately pH 7–8, whereas urea functionalization shifted the IEP to around pH 4, indicating a significant modification of the CNT surface chemistry. The urea–CNT and CNT–urea–CNT composites exhibited concentration-dependent antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli at 0.01–0.1 mg mL–1. The CNT–urea–CNT composite was more active against S. aureus at 0.05 and 0.1 mg mL–1, while the urea–CNT composite showed greater activity at 0.01 mg mL–1. The CNT–urea–CNT composite consistently exhibited stronger activity against E. coli, with a maximum inhibition zone of 33 ± 3.01 mm at 0.1 mg mL–1. These differences may reflect variations in surface structure, dispersion, and interactions with bacterial membranes.
